bugs.summary: CRAN checks could enforce Control Flow Integrity (KCFI) issues (e.g. from stale package_native_routine_registration_skeleton templates)
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
Some 40-50 CRAN packages have actual problems as identified by [`-fsanitize=kcfi`](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ControlFlowIntegrity.html#fsanitize-kcfi). Specifically, the settings for these 40-50 are `-fsanitize=kcfi -fsanitize-cfi-icall-generalize-pointers -fuse-ld=lld -Wl,-z,kcfi-trampolines`.

Take {dotCall64} for example, which has in [init.c](https://github.com/cran/dotCall64/blob/de0eca96011f215020f9624ed691b9399d7da371/src/init.c#L13): 

```
extern void dC64               ( void *);
```

But the implementation ([dotCall64.c](https://github.com/cran/dotCall64/blob/de0eca96011f215020f9624ed691b9399d7da371/src/dotCall64.c#L76)) is `SEXP dC64(SEXP)`:

```
SEXP dC64(SEXP args_in) {
  // ...
}
```

`ld.lld` will reject this under `-fsanitize=kcfi`.

That's a return-type mismatch; there are 3 other classes of issues that `-fsanitize=kcfi` can expose:

1. `const` mismatch, e.g. {caTools}

[caTools_init.c](https://github.com/cran/caTools/blob/21dec30aea222d6091b675302996bdd42b221935/src/caTools_init.c#L15) has:

```
extern void runmean(void *, void *, void *, void *);
```

[runfunc.c](https://github.com/cran/caTools/blob/21dec30aea222d6091b675302996bdd42b221935/src/runfunc.c#L270) has:

```
void runmean(double *In, double *Out, const int *nIn, const int *nWin)
```

KCFI preserves `const`-ness, so `ld.lld` rejects this

2. `()` vs. `(void)` mismatch, e.g. {hypergeo}

[init.c](https://github.com/cran/hypergeo/blob/38c15f391c2043eb3ce2c5cd7bfb21c8f16d021e/src/init.c#L17) has:

```
extern SEXP _hypergeo_RcppExport_registerCCallable();
```

[RcppExports.cpp](https://github.com/cran/hypergeo/blob/38c15f391c2043eb3ce2c5cd7bfb21c8f16d021e/src/RcppExports.cpp#L254) has:

```
RcppExport SEXP _hypergeo_RcppExport_registerCCallable()
```

Because this is C++, that means `(void)`! Hence the `ld.lld` rejection.

3. pointer-reference conflict, e.g. {cit}

[cit_init.c](https://github.com/cran/cit/blob/cf288c84f9c4c018339faea6859ccb2833af291a/src/cit_init.c#L10) has:

```
extern void citconlog2(void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *);
```

[citconlog2.cpp](https://github.com/cran/cit/blob/cf288c84f9c4c018339faea6859ccb2833af291a/src/citconlog2.cpp#L41-L42) has:

```
void citconlog2( double *L, double *G, double *T, int &nrow,
	int &ncol, double &pval, double &pval1, double &pval2, double &pval3, double &pval4, int &maxit )
```

`ld.lld` rejects equating `void *` with `int &`. The file also uses `extern "C"` earlier in the file to disable C++ name mangling, which disguises the issue from the normal linker.

----

NB: Many of the packages with issues are part of the set of about 600 packages on CRAN that failed to obey the `FIXME` emitted by `tools::package_native_routine_registration_skeleton()`:

```
/* FIXME:
Check these declarations against the C/Fortran source code.
*/
```

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Acran+%2FCheck+these+declarations+against+the+C%5C%2FFortran+source+code.%2F+%2Fvoid%5Cs*%5B*%5D%2F&type=code
comments.creator: michaelchirico4
michaelchirico4
comments.text: I sent out patches to the CRAN packages with return-type mismatches (~20), `()`-`(void)` mismatches (2), and pointer-reference conflicts (2); I ran out of steam to send out the other ~20 patches for `const` mismatch, with plans to return to this later.
